findings.title: Working-hours check rejects slots that fall outside any one of several working-hour ranges
findings.body:
The `workingHours.find(...)` returns true, meaning unavailable, as soon as any single working-hour entry for that weekday does not contain the slot.

Users with more than one range on the same day therefore lose slots. Examples:
- A split day such as 9–12 and 13–17.
- A schedule crossing UTC midnight, which `getWorkingHours` splits into two entries (e.g. 1020–1439 on day N and 0–60 on day N+1).

A slot inside one range is always outside the other, so it is rejected. The check must instead verify that the slot lies within at least one matching range. Otherwise US-timezone organizers, and anyone with split hours, can lose most or all slots.

findings.title: Working-hours end check uses slot start instead of slot end
findings.body: `end` is computed from `slotStartTime` (`slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()`), so it is identical to `start`. The `end > workingHour.endTime` comparison never detects a slot that starts inside working hours but runs past their end. It should use `slotEndTime`.

findings.title: Dayjs objects compared with === (always false)
findings.body: `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` compares two distinct object references, so it is always false. The intended 'override with zero length = unavailable all day' branch never runs. For such an override, a slot starting exactly at the override instant passes the remaining before/after checks and is treated as available. Use `.isSame()` instead.

findings.title: Slots overlapping the end of a date override are accepted
findings.body:
The only end-side rejection is `slotStartTime.isAfter(overrideEnd)`. Two cases slip through:
- A slot starting exactly at the override end.
- A slot that starts inside the override but ends after it, e.g. a 60-min slot starting 30 minutes before the end.

Both are considered available, so fixed hosts can still be booked outside their override window. The check should reject when `slotEndTime` is after the override end, or when `slotStartTime` is the same as or after it.

findings.title: Override date matching mixes server-local and UTC calendar days
findings.body:
Two problems in matching an override to a slot's day:
- The override day is computed with `dayjs(date.start)...format("YYYY MM DD")`, which uses the server's local timezone, while `slotStartTime` is UTC. On non-UTC servers the dates can mismatch.
- Matching is by UTC calendar day, not by the organizer's local day the override applies to. For organizers far from UTC (e.g. PST), regular-hours slots from the previous local day that share the UTC date get evaluated against the override and wrongly rejected. Conversely, override hours on the other UTC date are not matched.

findings.title: Shifted override minutes wrap around midnight and get dropped
findings.body: After adding the invitee/organizer offset, start and end are converted to minute-of-day via `hour()*60+minute()`. If the shift moves an override across the invitee's midnight (e.g. 22:00–02:00 in invitee time), endTime becomes smaller than startTime and `buildSlots` discards the range. `activeOverrides` is also still filtered on the unshifted `dayjs.utc(override.start)` date, so for large offsets the override can land on the wrong invitee day. Slots on the adjacent day are then missing or incorrect.

findings.title: Parsing Date.toString() output with dayjs is non-standard
findings.body: `dayjs(override.start.toString())` relies on `new Date()` parsing the locale-style string from `Date.toString()` (e.g. "Tue Mar 21 2023 ... GMT+0000 (Coordinated Universal Time)"). This format is implementation-defined and drops milliseconds. Passing the Date directly, `dayjs(override.start)`, is reliable.

findings.title: No test for the round-robin fixed-host date override fix
findings.body:
The PR's main fix is that fixed hosts' date overrides restrict round-robin availability, and it adds new override and working-hours logic to `checkIfIsAvailable`. Only a single-user timezone case is tested. Nothing covers:
- A round-robin event with fixed and loose hosts.
- Users with working hours crossing UTC midnight or split ranges.
- Slots overlapping override boundaries.

These are exactly the scenarios where the bugs above occur.
